title: THE RITUALS OF A DESPERATE PLAN

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Balaam said, "Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me." Balak did as Balaam said, and the two of them offered a bull and a ram on each altar. - Num 23:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The scheme against Israel now moves into its most religious phase. Balaam orders seven altars built and fourteen animals prepared for sacrifice. On the surface it looks like careful worship, elaborate and costly. But underneath, this is an attempt to bend God's hand toward a curse He has already forbidden.

Here is a sobering truth: religious activity can be used in the service of a wrong heart. Balak and Balaam went through all the motions of sacrifice, yet their aim was to oppose the purposes of God. The outward forms of devotion cannot sanctify a rebellious intention. God is not impressed by ceremony when the heart is set against Him.

This should make us examine our own worship. It is possible to sing, pray, and give while our hearts pursue something God has not blessed. Ritual without surrender is empty, however impressive it appears. The Lord looks past the seven altars to the heart behind them.

We should be grateful that in Christ we are not called to elaborate ceremonies to win God's favour. That favour was secured for us at the cross once and for all (Heb 10:12). True worship flows not from trying to manipulate God, but from a heart made new by grace. Let your worship be honest, offered from a heart that truly seeks Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Can religious activity ever mask a heart that is not surrendered to God?
2. Does your worship flow from genuine devotion or mere routine?
3. What would it mean to worship God with an honest, surrendered heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep my worship from becoming empty ritual. Give me a heart that truly seeks You, resting in the finished work of Christ rather than trying to earn Your favour. Amen.
